([[Chairman]] & [[Managing Director|MD]]) | revenue = | net_income = | assets = {{increase}}{{INRConvert|37560|m}} (2015-16) | production = {{convert|1756000|tonne|0}} | website = {{url|moil.nic.in}} }} '''MOIL''' (earlier known as '''Manganese Ore (India) Limited''') is a [[miniratna]] government [[manganese ore]] [[mining]] company headquartered in [[Nagpur]], [[India]]. With a market share of 50%, it is the largest producer of manganese ore in India.{{cite web|title=Production|url=http://ibm.nic.in/production.pdf|work=Indian Minerals Year Book 2008|publisher=Indian Bureau of Mines|accessdate=24 November 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721165807/http://ibm.nic.in/production.pdf|archivedate=21 July 2011}} MOIL operates 11 mines in adjoining districts of [[Maharashtra]] and [[Madhya Pradesh]]. It has been ranked #486 among the 500 top companies in India and 9th in the mines and metals sector of the [[Fortune India 500]] list for 2011.{{Cite web|url=http://www.indiainfoline.com/Markets/News/MOIL-enters-India-Fortune-500-List/5261381587|title=MOIL enters India Fortune 500 List}} In December 2010, the [[Government of India]] divested about 20% of its equity through an [[Initial public offering|IPO]]. Of the 20%, the Indian Government divested 10%, and the [[Government of Maharashtra]] and the [[Government of Madhya Pradesh]] each divested 5% of the total equity.{{cite news|title=MOIL Limited: IPO opens on Nov 26|url=http://www.centralchronicle.com/viewnews.asp?articleID=52203|accessdate=25 November 2010|newspaper=Central Chronicle|date=25 November 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125144800/http://www.centralchronicle.com/viewnews.asp?articleID=52203|archivedate=25 November 2010|df=dmy-all}}{{cite news|title=MOIL IPO on Nov 26|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/MOIL-IPO-on-Nov-26/Article1-628537.aspx|accessdate=25 November 2010|newspaper=Hindustan Times|date=19 November 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124094755/http://www.hindustantimes.com/MOIL-IPO-on-Nov-26/Article1-628537.aspx|archivedate=24 November 2010|df=dmy-all}} The central government holds 54% and the two state governments hold about 11% shares in MOIL.{{cite news|title=MOIL scouting for overseas mines ahead of IPO|url=http://www.tehelka.com/story_main47.asp?filename=Ws151110moil.asp|accessdate=25 November 2010|date=15 November 2010}} and the public holds about 35% shares. ==History== MOIL was originally set up as "Central Province Prospecting Syndicate" in the year 1896 in the region of [[Maharashtra]] and [[Madhya Pradesh]]. It was later renamed as "Central Provinces Manganese Ore Company Limited (CPMO)" in 1935. In 1962, the Government of India took over the mining activities from CPMO. Then, Manganese Ore (India) Limited was formed with 51% stake held between the Government of India and the Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh State governments. The other 49% was retained with CPMO. In 1977, the balance of 49% was acquired from CPMO, and MOIL became a 100% state-owned enterprise.{{cite news|title=IPO Analysis of Manganese Ore India Limited : Fairwealth Research|url=http://www.topnews.in/ipo-analysis-manganese-ore-india-limited-fairwealth-research-2293087|accessdate=25 November 2010|newspaper=Topnews.in|date=25 November 2010}} ==Mines== Eight of MOIL's eleven mines are underground mines (Kandri, Munsar, Beldongri, Gumgaon, Chikla, Balaghat, and Ukwa mines) and three are opencast mines (Dongri Buzurg, Sitapatore, and Tirodi). Its Balaghat mine is the largest of the 11 mines and the deepest at 383 metres.{{cite web|title=Preliminary Information Memorandum|url=http://steel.nic.in/MOIL_PIM_010503.PDF|publisher=Ministry of Steel|accessdate=25 November 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721174614/http://steel.nic.in/MOIL_PIM_010503.PDF|archive-date=21 July 2011|url-status=dead}} ==See also== * [[Fortune India 500]] * [[List of companies of India]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://moil.nic.in/ Official Website] * {{PM20|FID=co/054616|TEXT=Documents and clippings about|NAME=}} {{Public Sector Undertakings in India}} {{Nifty 200 companies}} {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Moil Limited}} [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:Mining companies of India]] [[Category:Companies based in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Mining in Maharashtra]] [[Category:1962 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1962]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Government-owned mining companies]]

MOIL (earlier known as Manganese Ore (India) Limited) is a miniratna government manganese ore mining company headquartered in Nagpur, India. With a market share of 50%, it is the largest producer of manganese ore in India. MOIL operates 11 mines in adjoining districts of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. It has been ranked #486 among the 500 top companies in India and 9th in the mines and metals sector of the Fortune India 500 list for 2011.
In December 2010, the Government of India divested about 20% of its equity through an IPO. Of the 20%, the Indian Government divested 10%, and the Government of Maharashtra and the Government of Madhya Pradesh each divested 5% of the total equity. The central government holds 54% and the two state governments hold about 11% shares in MOIL. and the public holds about 35% shares.
